correctness.rationale: Averaging the four printed circuit equations gives \(m_i=0\), \(m_2=-(g/h)m_1\), \(m_3=-(1+g/h)m_1\), and the cubic moment identity. On a nonnegative-support ergodic state, \(m_1=0\) would force a bounded complete support orbit to the origin. Jensen's inequality for the strictly convex map \(x^3\) on the half-line gives \(m_1\le\rho\), with equality only at the positive outer equilibrium. Finally, the zero mean of \(v_1(v_1^2-\rho^2)\) forces positive mass in both \((0,\rho)\) and \((\rho,\infty)\); otherwise invariance and continuity reduce the support to equilibrium levels. The negative statement follows by the vector-field inversion symmetry.
correctness.risk: The crossing conclusion is intentionally conditional on one-sided ergodic support; symmetric recurrent states can have zero barycenter and are not claimed to cross in this sense.

value.rationale: The equilibrium axis and outer-equilibrium voltage are intrinsic to this physical oscillator. Pinning every compact stationary barycenter to that axis and proving a sharp one-sided recurrence threshold gives a natural exact constraint on the multistable chaotic/hyperchaotic regimes studied in the source.

final_claim: For the cubic Clapp oscillator, every compact invariant probability measure has zero mean current, a barycenter on the line through the three equilibria, and the exact moment law \(\int v_1^3\,d\mu=\rho^2\int v_1\,d\mu\); every one-sided non-equilibrium ergodic state has mean strictly between the origin and the corresponding outer equilibrium and places positive mass on both sides of the outer-equilibrium voltage threshold.
limitations: The strict threshold conclusion requires ergodicity and one-sided support.
No claim is made for the source's piecewise-linear alternative model.
